title: Authorization, Ownership, RBAC & Permissions
outcome: Enforce resource ownership, workspace membership, roles, and permissions on the API with server-side policies.
artifact: Permission model + guards/policies protecting TaskFlow workspace/task actions with deliberate 401/403/404 semantics.
labSteps: List TaskFlow actions such as workspace.read, task.create, task.update, member.manage.
Map roles to capabilities without scattering role-name if statements across controllers.
Load membership for the relevant workspace and treat it as authorization evidence.
Enforce owner/member/role checks in server-side policy code.
Decide when 403 reveals too much and when a 404-style response better protects resource existence.
Write a matrix test covering at least owner, member, outsider, unauthenticated caller, and missing resource.
failureModes: Role strings checked inconsistently in every route
Checking membership after performing the mutation
IDOR: trusting a resource ID without proving caller access
mastery: Can model permission checks by action/resource
principles: Enforce ownership and role checks on the server even when the UI hides forbidden actions.
Model permissions around actions and resources instead of scattering role-name comparisons everywhere.
Check workspace membership before allowing resource operations tied to that workspace.
Use least privilege: a role should receive only the capabilities its workflows require.
